authorship.anchor_addition_rule: Design rule S-4, unchanged. A plausibility anchor may be added only where the feature is in the frozen vocabulary for that anchor study unit, is named by a cited claim as a presentation feature the candidate shares with the key or as a recognized reason to consider it, and is not on its own sufficient to satisfy that candidate's correctness conditions.
authorship.correctness_reading_rule: A newly admitted candidate's correctness conditions are a reading of its own frozen seed prose and of the cited claims, under the same disjunction rule the V2 readings use. No new clinical claim is authored.
authorship.no_llm_api: Discovery ran against the local Toronto Notes FTS5 index. Clinical reading is Claude Code interactive reasoning over retrieved and already admitted evidence.
authorship.refusal_rule: A candidate whose plausibility could only be asserted, not cited, is refused. So is a candidate that cannot state its correctness conditions in the frozen vocabulary, and so is one whose frozen prose records no state in which it would be correct. Refusals are recorded with their reason.
authorship.reuse_order: Cache first, then the curated contrast library, then already approved V2 relations, then the typed graph, then one bounded Toronto Notes full-text query, and authoritative evidence only where a claim was needed. Every admitted candidate in this wave came from the curated library or from an already frozen evidence packet; the graph and the full-text index contributed no concept that was not already there.
authorship.snapshot_rule: The pinned snapshot is FEATURE_ANCHOR_SNAPSHOT_V2 for every opportunity and is not rebuilt inside the pilot. A feature this wave would have needed and could not find is recorded as a proposed extension for the next snapshot and is invisible to every item in this batch.
authorship.what_this_is: One bounded acquisition wave for the six frozen medium-pilot opportunities. For each it records what discovery returned, the anchor or member acquired for each candidate, and an independent admissibility review of each. Nothing frozen is edited.

only_change: The distractor semantic class of the candidates the wave refused with V2_CANNOT_CARRY_A_NEVER_CORRECT_DISTRACTOR. No candidate was discovered, no anchor added, no evidence introduced and no other verdict moved.

proposed_extension_for_next_snapshot.blocked_by: Growing the frozen stem-feature vocabulary needs an evidence packet for the feature, and is outside this pilot's authorization.
proposed_extension_for_next_snapshot.normalized_feature: severe acute chest pain is the presenting complaint
proposed_extension_for_next_snapshot.why: It is the presentation every competitor in this set shares with the key and the reason a candidate considers an aortic cause at all. Without it dissection is expressible only as its own correctness conditions.

reasons: S-4 limb B fails. CLM-AORTIC-DISSECTION-01 names exactly three features as reasons to suspect acute aortic syndrome -- abrupt severe pain maximal at onset, pulse or blood-pressure differences, and malperfusion findings -- and all three are disjuncts of the competitor's own correctness tree, so each of them makes it correct rather than merely live.

No other feature in the frozen SU-C-21 vocabulary is named by any cited claim as a reason to consider dissection. The feature that would do the work is the severe acute chest pain the key and this competitor share, and the frozen 102-feature vocabulary has no feature for it; SU-C-21 states pain quality only as abrupt-maximal, pleuritic-positional or refluxlike.
Plausibility could only be asserted here, not cited, so the wave refuses rather than manufacturing an anchor.

candidates.why_it_belongs_to_the_learner_decision: CLM-AORTIC-DISSECTION-01 makes acute aortic syndrome a diagnosis to be settled in the same acute chest pain presentation, and the frozen seed review already admitted it.

added_anchors.s4_limb_b: CLM-R2-PED-DX-ANCHOR states the bronchiolitis prodrome as two to three days of fever, cough and rhinorrhea. Rhinorrhea is the nasal secretion suctioning addresses, and CLM-R4-PED-SUCTION is a claim about suctioning in exactly that illness. The coryzal prodrome is the presentation feature the candidate shares with the key.
added_anchors.s4_limb_c: The candidate's correctness condition is that nasal obstruction is limiting feeding or comfort. A coryzal prodrome is not that condition -- an infant may be coryzal without obstruction limiting feeds -- so the anchor makes the candidate live without making it correct.

review.clinical_plausibility: A coryzal infant with nasal secretions is the presentation in which clearing the nose is considered, and the frozen seed's own account of why a candidate would choose it turns on obligate nasal breathing.
review.second_key_risk: NONE. Nasal obstruction limiting feeds remains unstated and is the only thing that would make the option correct.

candidates.why_it_belongs_to_the_learner_decision: CLM-R4-PED-SUCTION is a bronchiolitis supportive-care claim about how suctioning should be done, in the same admitted infant.

reasons: S-4 limb B fails on every alternative. CLM-R4-PED-EPINEPHRINE is about admission rates and length of stay; it names no presentation feature at all, and certainly not the viral prodrome or the saturation.

The reason a candidate reaches for nebulized epinephrine in this infant is escalating work of breathing, which is already its anchor and is simultaneously the whole correctness condition of the high-flow competitor. That collision is a property of the set, not something an anchor can repair.

candidates.why_it_belongs_to_the_learner_decision: Already an admitted competitor; the wave was asked for a second anchor because its only presentation anchor is another competitor's whole correctness condition.
